set.origin: An older proverb, 'care'll kill a cat' (care meaning worry), appears in Ben Jonson's 1598 play; the 'curiosity' version is first recorded in the late 1860s.

why: Jonson's line is 'care'll kill a cat', not 'care killed the cat'; earliest 'curiosity' form is 1868, so 'by the late 1800s' is vague and 'began' overstated

set.def: very close or level in a race or contest, so that it is unclear who will win

why: 'exactly even' is wrong; the idiom means very close/level, not exactly tied; 'tied' removed from syn for the same reason

set.def: to barely manage to cope with a hard situation, especially money problems or too much work

why: 'just manage to survive' is ambiguous for learners ('just' = only?) and the money-only focus does not cover the homework cloze
'underdog' is not a synonym: an underdog is known and expected to lose; a dark horse is little known. Would be tested as the right answer to (e)

ex: Kwame keeps changing jobs and is never happy where he is; the grass is always greener on the other side.
City people dream of farm life and farmers dream of the city; the grass is always greener on the other side.

why: ex 1 'keeps changing jobs, but the grass is...' is illogical with 'but' and does not show the meaning
'Failing the first quiz was a blessing in disguise for Sofia, and she started studying' also fits the cloze sensibly
'arguing for it again would be rocking the boat' also fits the cloze
'jumped through hoops to make the interns feel welcome' fits the cloze; overlapping meaning (great effort)
'read between the lines before you share it' grammatically and plausibly fits the rumor-site cloze; related sense of not taking text at face value
cloze is about Yuki envying a friend's life, so 'green with envy' is a tempting near-fit; overlapping theme
'happy to pick his battles and let her run the shop' is a plausible fill; both involve stepping back
overlapping sense of doing more than needed; when in doubt remove
both mean 'no matter what / without stopping' for schedules ('open around the clock' vs 'open rain or shine'); near-overlap in (a)/(b)

cloze.s: A teenager was painting graffiti on the wall at midnight when the guard ___.

why: old cloze answer 'caught the teenager red-handed' required a word ('teenager') the sentence never gives

set.origin: An 18th-century story, possibly embellished, says playwright John Dennis devised new stage thunder for his 1709 play and protested when another production used it: 'That is my thunder!'

why: Dennis improved an existing thunder device rather than inventing the effect; the anecdote is poorly documented, so flag it as possibly embellished
